title: Bootstrap
subtitle: Methods in theoretical physics
overview: A workshop on bootstrap and related non-perturbative methods, bringing together researchers in quantum field theory, string theory, quantum gravity, and quantum information.

Through talks and informal discussions, we will explore how symmetry, unitarity, positivity, crossing symmetry, and analyticity constrain physical theories. The workshop connects analytic insights, numerical techniques, and exact results, with space for contributions from postdocs and students.

sessions.title: Moment approach to the SMEFT cone
Bootstrapping Lattice YM theory: from Euclidan to Hamiltonian formalism
sessions.abstract: We will first discuss the recent developments on bootstrapping Lattice Yang-Mills theory in the Euclidean path integral formalism and then the on-going work using the Hamiltonian Kogut-Susskind formalism.

sessions.title: Bootstrap in Hamiltonian Lattice Yang-Mills Theory
Maximal Giant Graviton Correlators in the 6d (2,0) Theory
sessions.abstract: We study four point functions of two maximal giant gravitons and two light half BPS operators in the 6d (2,0) theory. Treating the heavy operator pair as a zero dimensional defect, we use superconformal Ward identities to constrain the correlator at tree level in supergravity. Parisi Sourlas dimensional reduction organizes the bulk exchanges in terms of scalar seeds and leads us to propose a compact formula for arbitrary light Kaluza Klein levels. We test this results using the chiral bootstrap and the flat space limit.

sessions.title: Spinning Mellin Bootstrap
sessions.abstract: In this talk, I will show how to develop the Mellin formalism for spinning conformal correlators and use it to bootstrap AdS Yang-Mills theory and Einstein gravity. The key idea is that, kinematically, an n-point spinning correlator can be organized as a 2n-point scalar correlator. Based on this idea, I will introduce spinning Mellin amplitudes and derive their general pole structure, factorization properties, and flat space limit. I will then show how these ingredients, combined with conservation, fix tree-level amplitudes in AdS Yang-Mills theory and Einstein gravity through five points, and explain how the bootstrap can in principle be extended to arbitrary multiplicity.

sessions.title: No Particle Production and Integrability in AdS2
sessions.abstract: In two-dimensional flat spacetime, the absence of particle production is a hallmark of integrability. In this talk, I will discuss how this criterion can be generalized to AdS, where conventional scattering amplitudes are unavailable. We formulate an AdS analogue of no particle production through the absence of logarithmic singularities in holographic boundary correlators. Imposing this condition at arbitrary multiplicity uniquely selects the Liouville and Toda theories in AdS2. Along the way, we derive a simple all-point formula for AdS Berends–Giele currents and obtain closed-form expressions for boundary correlators. We also show that an independent approach based on higher-spin conserved currents leads to the same theories.

sessions.title: Defect correlation functions via bulk supergravity
sessions.abstract: We resolve a discrepancy between direct supergravity calculations and bootstrap results for defect two-point correlators, previously attributed to missing contact terms. We identify two sources of these contributions: nonlinear Kaluza–Klein field redefinitions that induce additional quadratic couplings to localized sources, and off-shell bulk–defect vertices that collapse internal defect propagators. We demonstrate that these mechanisms restore agreement in two examples of 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM: correlators in the presence of a $\frac12$-BPS Wilson line and on $\mathbb{RP}^4$.

sessions.title: Dimensional uplifts of thermal two-point functions and higher-derivative CFTs
(In Chinese) Bootstrapping mixed correlators in the 3d O(N) normal boundary universality class
sessions.abstract: 本报告介绍三维O(N)模型normal边界普适类的两点关联函数自举。我们采用基于η-最小化的截断共形自举方法求解边界交叉方程，重点研究了混合关联函数⟨𝜙S⟩。我们得到了一些算符标度量纲和展开系数的估计，并计算了其他重要普适量。新增的N=6数据进一步支持 extraordinary-log边界普适类的稳定性阈值Nc≈5这一结论。通过比较不同算符给出的位移算符Zamolodchikov范数的估计，我们检验了自举结果的自洽性。此外，我们考察了若干共形数据随N的变化，并与大N展开的解析预测进行了比较。

sessions.title: Topologically Twisted Indices for ABJM at Finite N via Algebraic Geometry & Black Hole Microstates in AdS4
sessions.abstract: Understanding the microscopic origin of black hole entropy is a central goal of quantum gravity. The AdS/CFT correspondence provides a natural framework for addressing this problem through supersymmetric partition functions of dual field theories. Supersymmetric localization is a powerful non-perturbative method in quantum field theory that enables exact computations of protected observables at strong coupling. In this talk, I will first introduce the topologically twisted index (TTI) of the 3d ABJM theory at finite rank and Chern–Simons level k=1. The construction builds on the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs), which is carried out using two alternative methods, both relying on techniques from algebraic geometry. Under specific identifications among the magnetic fluxes and chemical potentials, these methods yield finite-rank results for N=2,…,22. These indices are then compared with their large-N counterparts. Finally, I will present holographic comparisons between the Laurent expansion of the TTI at finite N as a function of its fugacity and the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy of the dual magnetic and dyonic supersymmetric AdS_4 black holes.

sessions.title: OPE Coefficients of the E-series Minimal Models
sessions.abstract:
I will discuss the OPE coefficients of the ADE Virasoro minimal models, reviewing both known results and new results focusing on E series.

I will first explain how the OPE coefficients can be partially derived by making use of additional non-invertible symmetry. This provides a particularly efficient way to organize the operator algebra and makes several structures in the answer transparent.

I will then ask how much of this additional structure is actually necessary. I will show that the full set OPE coefficients can be determined from conformal bootstrap, assuming only Virasoro symmetry, permutation symmetry, and OPE associativity. The key idea is that the conformal bootstrap problem for infinitely many models can be reduced to a finite algebraic problem governed by quantum-group 6j symbols. The finite problem is then solved by computer.

The talk is based on the recent work with Amaury Lhoste and Masahito Yamazaki, arXiv: 2609.25215.

sessions.title: Thermal Polyakov bootstrap
sessions.abstract: We derive thermal Polyakov bootstrap equations for CFT two-point functions on S^1 times R^{d−1}. Combining the thermal OPE with a dispersion relation and the method of images gives a representation in blocks that satisfy Kubo–Martin–Schwinger (KMS) co-variance. Their local expansions contain additional thermal blocks at classical double-twist dimensions. Matching the prescribed physical OPE requires cancellation of these generated contributions, yielding explicit linear equations for thermal OPE coefficients, including any compensating terms required by the reconstruction. We formulate the equations for bosonic scalar correlators and antiperiodic scalar structures extracted from fermion correlators, and find consistent solutions in analytically tractable thermal CFTs. The coefficient matrix, which we call the Polyakov matrix, connects the large-spin expansion to KMS consistency and reduces to minus the identity on the classical double-twist spectrum. This structure suggests a numerical approach to the three-dimensional Ising CFT that combines known low-lying vacuum data with a self-consistent large-spin tail.

sessions.title: Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
sessions.abstract:
Tinghong Shen (Southeast University)
Based on work with Zhijin Li: arXiv:2606.09985 and arXiv:2611.20214

Whether the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) is a genuine unitary conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by walking near complex fixed points has been an outstanding puzzle for two decades. We address this question by combining the conformal bootstrap with fuzzy-sphere spectroscopy.

Under suitable sparseness assumptions, the SO(5) bootstrap bound develops a sharp cone whose apex sits remarkably close to large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) estimates. Incorporating mixed correlators of the three lowest scalars $\phi$, $s$, and $t$, we extract the spectrum and OPE coefficients across nine SO(5) representations. On the fuzzy sphere, symmetry projection extends exact diagonalization up to $N = 12$ Landau orbitals, and conformal lowering identifies 52 primaries at $N = 10$, of which 31 were previously unclassified.

The three methods show striking quantitative concordance: the bootstrap singlet dimension $\Delta_s = 2.258$ closely matches QMC’s $2.273(4)$; OPE ratios agree with the fuzzy sphere to within $0.3\%\text{--}0.7\%$; and beyond the 23 previously established fuzzy-sphere primaries that already exhibit close agreement with the bootstrap, 16 of the newly identified primaries are successfully predicted in the accessible channels. Together, these results provide comprehensive evidence for the multicriticality scenario of the SO(5) DQCP.

sessions.title: Positivity bounds in effective field theories beyond tree level
sessions.abstract: In an effective field theory (EFT) with an analytic, unitary ultraviolet (UV) completion, positivity bounds often translate into simple sign constraints on Wilson coefficients at tree level. This connection becomes more obscure when loop effects are important. In a scalar EFT, explicit matching can yield a negative Wilson coefficient for a dimension-eight operator first generated at one loop in the UV theory. Loops involving dimension-four and dimension-six operators also enter the forward dispersion relation at this order, and the sum of all contributions remains positive. The optical theorem relates a cut of the one-loop amplitude to interference between the contact and heavy-particle exchange amplitudes. This interference can contribute to the total cross section with either sign. In scalar electrodynamics with a weakly coupled UV completion whose heavy particles have spin at most one, the photon–scalar coefficient can likewise violate its tree-level bound at the matching scale. In photon–photon scattering, gauge invariance pushes competing contributions from other operators beyond one loop in the UV theory, so both four-photon bounds hold through that order.

sessions.title: Bootstrapping Symmetries in Many-body systems
sessions.abstract: Symmetries shape the spectra and dynamics of quantum many-body systems, yet identifying hidden symmetries remains challenging. In this talk, I will present a bootstrap framework that starts from a known symmetry subgroup and uses the cross spectral form factor (xSFF) to probe correlations between its symmetry sectors. Combining these spectral data with algebraic consistency conditions enables the reconstruction of representation-theoretic data of hidden finite-group symmetries, including branching rules, fusion rules, and character tables, without explicitly constructing the hidden symmetry operators. I will illustrate the framework in interacting lattice models, explain its applicability to both chaotic and integrable systems, and outline an ancilla-assisted randomized-measurement protocol for accessing the xSFF experimentally. If time permits, I will conclude with ongoing extensions to open quantum systems and projective representations, including applications to identifying information preserved under noise.
